402252.title: Court Music Ensemble Regular Concert: Yeongsan Hoesang
402252.overview:
Yeongsan Hoesang is the essence of pungnyu, the refined chamber music of Korea's literati. Over centuries of performance and transmission it grew from a song into instrumental music, and from a single melody into a suite of pieces, constantly changing in instrumentation, register and playing style.

It has changed for hundreds of years without ever disappearing. The National Gugak Center's Court Music Ensemble traces that long evolution in this regular concert.

407029.title: STILL: Paek Yunzo and Tatsuhito Horikoshi
407029.overview:
A two-person show (12 November – 5 December 2026) pairing Paek Yunzo (b. 1980) and the Tokyo-based Tatsuhito Horikoshi (b. 1985). The title plays on two meanings: a frozen moment, and a state that still continues.

Paek captures everyday figures walking, standing or carrying animals and objects, in spare lines and bright colour on broad monochrome grounds, with a dry wit. Horikoshi, trained in Western painting at Tama Art University, draws on anime and manga to paint boys and girls in classical portrait poses, using fine brushwork and complementary colour to give them an unreal air. His work sold out on its Korean debut at KIAF Seoul 2023.

407969.title: Im Hyun-hee Solo Exhibition: Water Light
407969.overview:
Im Hyun-hee paints her reflections on life and self. Her work resembles nature in the way it lets different sensations coexist in a single flow rather than setting them apart or against each other.

Chance encounters with nature long fed her practice, but finding that loose, intuitive work too faint to hold an evolving inner story, she began exploring new approaches. In the new paintings, force radiates outward from a centre, leaving layered traces of colour and material that carry movement and flow.

The Water Light Seeping series, shown here for the first time, marks the start of this new direction: less about reproducing a moment in nature, more about an inward process that ends in nature-like painting.

402253.price: S seats ₩30,000; A seats ₩20,000; B seats ₩10,000
402253.overview:
The National Gugak Center's Folk Music Ensemble gave its first folk music concert on 9–10 June 1981 at the National Theater's small hall in Jangchung-dong, arranging vocal music for instruments and solos for ensemble so that folk instrumental music could reach a wider public.

This regular concert presents the works that grew from those beginnings into signature pieces of folk ensemble playing: Namdo Gutgeori, Seongju Puri and Yukjabaegi, along with sanjo.
